'''Ariel Fernandez''' (born '''Ariel Fernández Stigliano''', April 8, 1957) is an Argentinian–American [[physical chemist]] and [[pharmaceutical]] researcher.<ref name="CV">{{cite journal|url=https://www.academia.edu/6141377|title=Ariel Fernandez CV and Biographical Narrative|author=Ariel Fernandez|journal=Academia.edu}}</ref> 

In 2025, a judge determined that Fernandez had engaged in [[scientific misconduct]], and in 2026 he was barred from receiving federal research funding in the US for 15 years. Fernandez denies the misconduct findings.<ref name="retraction2"/>

==Education==
Fernandez received [[Licentiate (degree)|licentiate]] degrees in chemistry (1979) and mathematics (1980) from the [[Universidad Nacional del Sur]], Argentina.<ref name="CV" /> He then earned a [[Ph.D.]] from [[Yale University]] in 1984 with a thesis entitled ''Structural Stability of Chemical Systems at Critical Regimes''.<ref name="CV" /><ref name=Diss>Ariel Fernandez. [http://hdl.handle.net/10079/bibid/9852978 Yale University Dissertation: Structural Stability of Chemical Systems at Critical Regimes (Dissipative Structures, Potential Energy Surfaces)] Published/Created:1984</ref>

==Career==
Fernandez held the Karl F. Hasselmann Professorship of Bioengineering at [[Rice University]] from 2006 until 2011 when he left as part of a settlement of a research misconduct investigation by the university.<ref name=Retraction /> 

Fernandez developed the concept of the dehydron, an adhesive structural defect in a soluble [[protein]] that promotes its own [[solvation shell|dehydration]].<ref>{{cite journal |journal=[[Physics (magazine)|Physics]] |last=Monroe |first=Dan |title=Proteins Hook up Where Water Allows |year=2012 |volume=5 |issue=51 |page=51 |doi=10.1103/Physics.5.51 |bibcode=2012PhyOJ...5...51M |url=http://physics.aps.org/articles/v5/51 |accessdate=June 23, 2021}}</ref> The [[Conserved sequence|nonconserved]] nature of protein dehydrons has implications for [[drug discovery]], as dehydrons may be targeted by highly specific drugs/ligands.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Crunkhorn |first=Sarah |title=Anticancer drugs: Redesigning kinase inhibitors |year=2008 |journal=[[Nature Reviews Drug Discovery]] |volume=7 |pages=120–121 |doi=10.1038/nrd2524 |s2cid=27083179 |url=https://www.nature.com/nrd/journal/v7/n2/full/nrd2524.html|url-access=subscription }}</ref> This technology was applied by Fernandez and collaborators to design a new compound based on the anticancer drug [[Gleevec]], in order to reduce its [[cardiotoxicity]].<ref>Demetri G. D. Structural reengineering of imatinib to decrease cardiac risk in cancer therapy.2007 Dec 3;  J Clin Invest. 117(12):3650–3653. doi  10.1172/JCI34252 [https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC2096446/]</ref><ref name="Dunham">Dunham W. Reworked Gleevec curbs heart-related complication. REUTERS December 3, 2007 [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-cancer-gleevec-idUSN0341290220071203]</ref>

===Misconduct findings===
The editorial board of the ''[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America|Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences]]'' [[Retraction in academic publishing|retracted]] a January 2006 paper coauthored by Fernandez because it had "substantial overlap", without attribution, of figures and text from an article by Fernandez published in ''[[Structure (journal)|Structure]]'' the previous month, a form of [[duplicate publication]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=Retraction for Fernández et al., Packing defects as selectivity switches for drug-based protein inhibitors|first=Nicholas R.|last=Cozzarelli|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, USA|volume=103|issue=11|page=4329|date=March 14, 2006|doi=10.1073/pnas.0601034103|pmid=16505348 |pmc=1449696 |bibcode=2006PNAS..103.4329C |doi-access=free }}</ref> An [[expression of concern]] was issued  in 2013 by the editors of ''[[BMC Genomics]]'' about a 2011 paper published there by Fernandez.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/1471-2164-14-260|title=Erratum to: Expression of concern: subfunctionalization reduces the fitness cost of gene duplication in humans by buffering dosage imbalances|journal=BMC Genomics|volume=14|article-number=260|date=April 17, 2013}}</ref> In 2014, geneticist [[Michael Lynch (geneticist)|Michael Lynch]] asked the editors of [[Nature (journal)|''Nature'']] to remove his name from a 2011 paper he had coauthored with Fernandez, leading the editors there to also publish an expression of concern.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nature13141|title=Editorial Expression of Concern: Non-adaptive origins of interactome complexity|journal=Nature|volume=516|page=440|date=2014}}</ref>

The [[United States Office of Research Integrity]] (ORI) opened an investigation in 2010 and determined in 2022 that Fernandez had falsified research findings "in 12 published papers, four unpublished manuscripts, one presentation, and three grant applications". ORI proposed a 15-year [[debarment]] sanction by the [[United States Department of Health and Human Services|US Department of Health and Human Service]].<ref name=Retraction/><ref name="retraction2" /> In May 2025, an [[administrative law judge]] reviewing that report found that Fernandez's "research misconduct squandered Rice and NIH funds", referring to $1.2 million in grant funding, and recommended upholding the proposed debarment.<ref name=Retraction>{{Cite web |last=Gallegos |first=Alicia |date=2026-03-26 |title=Judge upholds 15-year debarment against scientist who once threatened to sue Retraction Watch |url=https://retractionwatch.com/2026/03/26/ariel-fernandez-chemist-rice-ori-hhs-alj-debarment/ |access-date=2026-03-29 |website=Retraction Watch |language=en-US}}</ref> In May 2026, ORI formally debarred Fernandez for scientific misconduct, for a period of fifteen years, finding that he intentionally fabricated data.<ref name="retraction2">{{cite web |last1=Gallegos |first1=Alicia |title=ORI announces 15-year debarment against former Rice University scientist |url=https://retractionwatch.com/2026/05/04/ori-announces-15-year-debarment-against-former-rice-university-scientist/ |website=Retraction Watch |publisher=The Center for Scientific Integrity |access-date=2026-05-05}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Findings of Research Misconduct |url=https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/05/2026-08675/findings-of-research-misconduct |website=Federal Register |publisher=The Office of the Federal Register |access-date=2026-05-05}}</ref>
